captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 5. In this lesson: When the city wakes up.
Recognise personification in a poem.
Here are some new words. Personification. Describing a thing as if it were a person.
Stretch. Make your body long to wake it up. Yawn. Open your mouth wide when you are tired.
Listen and say them. personification
stretch
yawn.
And some more words. Hum. Make a low, steady sound. Rush. Move or do something very quickly.
Dawn. The time when the sun comes up. Listen and say them. hum
rush
dawn.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: describing a thing as if it were a person?
Now some grammar: Personification.
Personification gives human actions or feelings to things that are not human.
For example: The wind whispered through the trees.
For example: The old car coughed and stopped.
Now listen, and read along. City morning. At dawn the city stretches and yawns,
The streetlights blink their sleepy eyes, The buses cough and rumble awake,
And windows open to the skies. The traffic hums a busy song, The bakery breathes out warm,
sweet bread, The river rushes off to work – And I'm still lying in my bed!
Another question. The video will stop. When does the poem take place?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like personification, stretch, yawn.
You practised personification. And you read City morning. Now try the practice questions.
See you next time!

q.prompt: How many syllables are in the first line of a haiku?

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 5. In this lesson: Haiku and syllables.
Count syllables and choose synonyms for stronger words.
Here are some new words. Haiku. A short Japanese-style poem of 5, 7 and 5 syllables.
Syllable. A part of a word with one vowel sound, like ba, na, na. Synonym.
A word with the same or nearly the same meaning. Listen and say them. haiku
syllable
synonym.
And some more words. Petal. One of the coloured parts of a flower. Ripple.
A small wave on water. Shimmer. Shine with a soft, moving light. Listen and say them. petal
ripple
shimmer.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: a short Japanese-style poem of 5, 7 and 5 syllables?
Now some grammar: Synonyms for stronger writing.
A synonym can make writing more exact and interesting. ‘Big’ can be huge, enormous or vast.
‘Said’ can be whispered, shouted or replied.
For example: a big wave becomes an enormous wave.
For example: a nice day becomes a glorious day.
Now listen, and read along. Four seasons in haiku. Spring.
Pink petals falling, the old tree shakes off winter – a soft pink snowstorm. Summer.
Hot sand burns my feet, the sea pulls me with cool hands, ripples shimmer gold. Autumn.
Red leaves on the path, the wind gathers them like coins and throws them away. Winter.
Silent white morning, my breath paints clouds in the air, the pond is a mirror.
Another question. The video will stop. How many syllables are in the first line of a haiku?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like haiku, syllable, synonym.
You practised synonyms for stronger writing. And you read Four seasons in haiku.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
